title: debian: Check if including wsutil public headers compile
description:
without headers from libwiretap or libwireshark.

Improves #20901.

Marked as draft, since the check fails until #20901 is fixed.

notes.body: Perhaps there should be a Debian packaging check, but there should probably also be a test done on *all* build platforms as part of the build process.

The problems I found so far affected all platforms, but indeed, there can be platform specific problems with the headers that would be caught only by running similar checks on all platforms. I think those are more rare though, thus having the check on at least one platform catches most of the issues with the headers.
@geraldcombs In the CI for merges this check is not running leading to breakages slipping in to be caught in the nightly Ubuntu builds and in GitHub actions. Since header issues seem to be common recently how about adding a similar check to the GitLab Ubuntu GCC build or replacing it with a full package build to have this check run and guard master?

While #20901 is resolved this check still fails:

```
In file included from <stdin>:1:
debian/libwsutil-dev/usr/include/wireshark/cfile.h:15:10: fatal error: epan/epan.h: No such file or directory
   15 | #include <epan/epan.h>
      |          ^~~~~~~~~~~~~
compilation terminated.
make[1]: *** [debian/rules:99: override_dh_install] Error 1
```
In `packaging/debian/libwsutil-dev.install` the top level headers are installed in `libwsutil-dev` and those include headers from libwireshark-dev, which is wrong, because `libwsutil-dev` does not and should not depend on `libwireshark-dev`.

I'm not sure what will be the right solution, but probably each top level header should move to either `epan/` `wsutil/` or `wiretap/`.
Does !23009 help?  I got suspicious when cfile.h wasn't included in any wsutil files.

Looks like there is a little more work to go, but I agree with the statement that cfile.h should not be included in any epan headers.  Currently it's used in 2 places:
1. plugin_if.h - See #11968 for the current discussion about that (no need to duplicate here)
2. secrets.h - The problem is interaction with modifying a capture (PCAPNG) file with decryption data (that was decrypted in a dissector).  Not sure of the best way to break that all up cleanly between epan (that holds the dissector data), wiretap (that handling PCAPNG files), and ui (that initiates the export process of writing the decryption data).
To not potentially duplicate work, I'll investigate fixing plugin_if.  The secret.h issue is probably best done by @Lekensteyn or @guyharris
Cleanup of plugin_if.h done in !23019
cfile.h should now be out of the epan directory.
While cfile.h is not included in any epan headers, cfile.h itself includes a lot of epan headers, so I'm not sure how much that helps.

```
$ ln -s packaging/debian
$ dpkg-buildpackage -d
...
In file included from <stdin>:1:
debian/libwsutil-dev/usr/include/wireshark/cfile.h:15:10: fatal error: epan/epan.h: No such file or directory
   15 | #include <epan/epan.h>
      |          ^~~~~~~~~~~~~
compilation terminated.
$ git log --oneline -2
597d702e05 (HEAD -> check-independent-wsutil-headers) debian: Check if including wsutil public headers compile
e4c2561a6e GitLab CI: macOS updates
```

The only shared library that has header files that include `cfile.h` is libuiqt-plugin.

libuiqt-plugin wants pointers to a number of structs from epan and `cfile.h` (so opaque types might be ok), and also wants the `file_state` enum. `cfile.h` also pulls into a bunch of other headers itself, mostly from epan but also from wiretap, though epan already depends on wiretap. We probably could, especially in the short term, move `cfile.h` into epan.
I don't want to push any short-term solution, I'm fine landing this when everything got in the right place.
I looked at it some more and I'm not sure it would be possible at all to try to remove the epan dependencies from `cfile.h`. So I think !24552 is the right answer.

Where I'm confused is where/why wsutil (or libwsutil) needs cfile.h if none of its files include it (since af71d884).  As @johnthacker stated, it's only used by the libuiqt-plugin, which should be very separate from wsutil, but libuiqt-plugin is obviously required to build the wireshark UI.  I was really trying to avoid having cfile.h in epan because I think it's a mix of backend/UI layers and I want to minimize the "UI" layer in epan as much as possible. I liked it in the main folder just because it was a mix and didn't really have a "library home".

It's mostly a packaging issue. On a Linux system, say, `/usr/include/wireshark` gets created.

There are sub-directories uiqt/ epan/ wiretap/ and wsutil/ that get installed by libuiqt-plugin, libwireshark, libwiretap, and libwustil, respectively. There are also include files not associated with any particular one of those libraries that are just in `/usr/include/wireshark` (and `c128/`).

Shared libraries (unlike static) have to form a directed acyclic graph. libuiqt-plugin depends on libwireshark, which depends on libwiretap, which depends on libwsutil, which depends on the files in the wireshark root that don't really belong to any of the shared libraries but to a common base. (Also some of the earlier ones in that list depend on later ones, like all the earlier ones depend on libwsutil. That's fine, it doesn't create a cycle.)

Since `cfile.h` includes libwireshark headers, it has to go in either libwireshark or libuiqt-plugin, otherwise it would create a cycle. But most of the executables depend on cfile.h, so if it went into libuiqt-plugin, it would make the executables depend on libuiqt-plugin, which wouldn't make sense. So `cfile.h` has to belong to libwireshark. You can't install `cfile.h` in the root directory unless you have something kind of odd where you say it "belongs" to libwireshark but, unlike all other libwireshark files, ends up in the root. You *could* do that, but it's probably more confusing.

libuiqt-plugin already depends on libwireshark, even without moving cfile.h in there, so this is no real change.
Very likely at some point after this change, @rbalint would like to further fine tune it and have a check that nothing in libwiretap depends on anything in libwireshark.

There are some header files in the root directory that don't have to get installed as public headers, and aren't. `cfile.h` isn't one of them - it gets used by `libuiqt-plugin` (and was by those files when they were in epan/libwireshark), so it *has* to be installed.

Speaking of checking whether public headers work, would CMake's [`VERIFY_INTERFACE_HEADER_SETS`](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/prop_tgt/VERIFY_INTERFACE_HEADER_SETS.html) be useful?
Oh, that is interesting.

Yeah, that popped up today when I was checking my pile of RSS feeds; one of the feeds is Planet KDE, and [a blog post with the title "C++ Library Headers & CMake Config Files: Are We Serviceable?"](https://frinring.wordpress.com/2026/06/30/c-library-headers-cmake-config-files-are-we-serviceable/) showed up.

I was curious what "serviceable" meant in that context, so I checked it in the RSS reader, and saw that. First I'd ever heard of [`VERIFY_INTERFACE_HEADER_SETS`](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/prop_tgt/VERIFY_INTERFACE_HEADER_SETS.html).

 	-Idebian/libwireshark-dev/usr/include \
